edges.effect_quant: Pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest a small average effect that is directionally consistent but not dramatic.
edges.mechanism: The proposed pathway combines changes in oxidative damage, inflammatory tone, hormone signaling, bile-acid metabolism, and exposure to food-derived carcinogens or protective phytochemicals. For Bladder cancer, those pathways matter over years, so consistent long-term intake patterns are more informative than short interventions.
edges.summary: Cruciferous vegetables appears tied to lower risk of bladder cancer in general adult mainly through pooled meta-analytic evidence. The likely magnitude is modest, which is why the edge is framed conservatively rather than as a headline-level breakthrough.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
